gap: Character fidelity at medium-shot range (image B). In a chest-height shot about 2.5 m from the walker, a crop of his head and torso must show all of the following. (1) Skin micro-detail: pores, stubble and creases at the eyes and mouth, with soft subsurface shading and a readable expression, not smooth uniform orange. (2) Hair broken into strands and clumps with directional highlights, not a solid shell. (3) A shirt with visible weave or pattern, seams and stitching, plus folds that shift with the stride. Passes when that crop matches A's face and flannel in material richness.
notes:
better_than_baseline=true. Baseline: BLIND VERDICT vs GTA V: OURS LOSES in all 4 pairs (we are B in each). Wowed: no. GTA V wins on character fidelity (cloth folds, faces, expressive weight-bearing poses), scene density and lighting. Our character has a smooth doll-like face and plain shirt and stands in a barren plaza. On motion itself, our walk, jog and sprint now read as real gaits, but they lack GTA V's foot locking, start and pivot transitions, and believable jumps.

BASELINE COMPARISON (progress/img/integration/C, plus headless metrics from the main checkout 8bccbd7; its player.gd and character_visual.gd match the merge-base 8595a12):
- Gameplay photos 01-07: same world, lighting, HUD and camera framing. Only the player pose differs: shots 01 and 02 now hold a mid-stride pose through the photo fixture, so they are posed, not live motion. No world regression in any of the 7 views.
- Baseline gaits: there was only one run clip. Walk input still ran at 3.6 m/s on that clip at 0.9x, and sprint was the same clip at 1.36x. Steps were short shuffles (0.8 m at 4.4-4.7 steps/s) with about 3% flight. Ankle lateral separation was 0.27 m, wider than the 0.21 m hip joints (the splayed legs the owner complained about). Idle ankle separation was 0.29 m.
- Our gaits: separate walk, run and sprint clips, each at rate 1.0 in steady state:

| Gait | Speed | Cycle | Cadence | Ankle separation | Flight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Walk | 1.5 m/s | 1.00 s | 120 steps/min | 0.12 m | 0% |
| Run | 3.6 m/s | 0.73 s | 164 steps/min | 0.11 m | 37-42% |
| Sprint | 6.8 m/s | 0.63 s | 190 steps/min | 0.10 m | 53-57% |

- Also new: idle ankle separation 0.20 m, a 0.6 s stop clip, and jump_start/land clips on standing jumps. Aim-walk planted-foot slip dropped from 0.68 m/s to 0.07 m/s.
- Unchanged from baseline: jump apex 1.14 m and 0.60 s airtime; strafing and backpedalling while aiming still slide the feet (2.4-3.4 m/s ours, 2.9-3.3 m/s baseline).
- No regression found: --test 140/140 (84e1b8f), headless route 13/13 (5bf9944), 7 gameplay views.

Both owner complaints are fixed in the rendered frames: walking and running are no longer a sped-up clip, and the legs are no longer too far apart. Real side and behind contact sheets confirm it. Remaining motion flaws, all measured from my own skeleton logs:
- Planted-foot slip, median: 0.23 m/s walk, 0.44 m/s run, 0.94 m/s sprint. At sprint the 90th percentile is 2.3 m/s, and the foot skids in at about 3 m/s for 2 frames at touchdown.
- Standstill to walk reaches full speed in about 0.14 s, with no start step.
- The sharp 180 from a sprint is a rotation while the legs keep cycling (walk clip at 1.25x for about 0.3 s), with no plant or skid.
- Sprint stop is a single braking step from 5.7 m/s.
- Jumps are floaty and frozen (details under the gap).

Judge: Image A wins all four pairs clearly and none is close. The four B frames share one profile, and none of them wows. The ground is a barren, uniformly tiled plaza with repeated stain decals and no pedestrians, traffic or street furniture near the subject, so roughly half of every frame is dead space. The character is low-fidelity: waxy uniform skin, solid-mass hair and flat-colour clothing, which is fatal in the two medium shots. The pose is stiff in the upper body: an upright torso, minimal arm counter-swing and, in the run frame, one hand frozen at chin height. A world-space 'Kampong Sirih Road' label floats over the real sign and reads as debug UI. Composition is weak, with a small centred subject and no foreground framing element. B has real assets to build on: pleasant golden-hour light with long soft shadows, convincingly weathered housing blocks and car-park podium, and atmospheric distance haze. On locomotion specifically, the B stance width looks normal (feet near the line of travel), and the run frame shows a genuine flight/kick-back phase rather than a sped-up walk. Still, neither the walk nor the run has the weight transfer, forward lean or loose arm swing that A's walkers show. In order of priority, B needs: dense street dressing and life around the player; character skin, hair and cloth shading that holds up at 2 to 2.5 m; a run with forward lean and pumping arms instead of a held hand; and removal of the floating label. Of the A frames, the fire-backed walk (pair 1) and the sunlit bat confrontation (pair 4) are genuine wows. The leaning-on-car shot (pair 3) is polished but staged, and the alley walk (pair 2) is strongly composed but on clearly dated textures.
